<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
b.d6701fb4da:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship Him.

b.bf664075f6:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>C</c>hriste Redémptor ómnium,
Ex Patre Patris únice,
Solus ante princípium
Natus ineffabíliter.

<h>T</h>u lumen, tu splendor Patris,
Tu spes perénnis ómnium:
Inténde quas fundunt preces
Tui per orbem fámuli.

<h>M</h>eménto salútis Auctor,
Quod nostri quondam córporis,
Ex illibáta Vírgine
Nascéndo, formam súmpseris.

<h>S</h>ic præsens testátur dies,
Currens per anni círculum,
Quod solus a sede Patris
Mundi salus advéneris.

<h>H</h>unc cælum, terra, hunc mare,
Hunc omne quod in eis est,
Auctórem advéntus tui,
Laudans exsúltat cántico.

<h>N</h>os quoque, qui sancto tuo
Redémpti sánguine sumus,
Ob diem natális tui,
Hymnum novum concínimus.

<h>G</h>lória tibi Dómine,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
b.a59f7df07b:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>J</c>esus, the Ransomer of man,
Who, ere created light began,
Didst from the sovereign Father spring,
His power and glory equalling.

<h>T</h>he Father’s Light and Splendor Thou,
Their endless hope to Thee that bow;
Accept the prayers and praise to-day
That through the world Thy servants pay.

<h>S</h>alvation’s Author, call to mind
How, taking form of humankind,
Born of a Virgin undefiled,
Thou in man’s flesh becam’st a Child.

<h>T</h>hus testifies the present day,
Through every year in long array,
That Thou, salvation’s source alone,
Proceedest from the Father’s throne.

<h>T</h>he heavens above, the rolling main
And all that earth’s wide realms contain,
With joyous voice now loudly sing
The glory of their new-born King.

<h>A</h>nd we who, by Thy precious Blood
From sin redeemed, are marked for God,
On this the day that saw Thy birth,
Sing the new song of ransomed earth.

<h>O</h> Lord, the Virgin-born, to Thee
Eternal praise and glory be,
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.
Amen.

<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:

<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who, by the fruitful virginity of the Blessed Mary, hast given unto mankind the rewards of everlasting life; grant, we beseech thee, that we may continually feel the might of her intercession, through whom we have worthily received the Author of our life, our Lord Jesus Christ, thy Son:
<h>W</h>ho with thee liveth and reigneth, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.4837995ac4:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Heb 1:1-2</r>
<c>M</c>ultifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>A</c> solis ortus cárdine
Ad usque terræ límitem,
Christum canámus Príncipem,
Natum María Vírgine.

<h>B</h>eátus Auctor sǽculi
Servíle corpus índuit:
Ut carne carnem líberans,
Ne pérderet quos cóndidit.

<h>C</h>astæ Paréntis víscera
Cæléstis intrat grátia:
Venter Puéllæ báiulat
Secréta, quæ non nóverat.

<h>D</h>omus pudíci péctoris
Templum repénte fit Dei:
Intácta nésciens virum,
Verbo concépit Fílium.

<h>E</h>níxa est puérpera,
Quem Gábriel prædíxerat,
Quem matris alvo géstiens,
Clausus Ioánnes sénserat.

<h>F</h>œno iacére pértulit:
Præsépe non abhórruit:
Parvóque lacte pastus est,
Per quem nec ales ésurit.

<h>G</h>audet chorus cæléstium,
Et Angeli canunt Deo;
Palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

<h>G</h>lória tibi Dómine,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini.
<r>℟.</r> Deus Dóminus, et illúxit nobis.
b.4dc0ced7fb:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Heb 1:1-2</r>
<c>G</c>od, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>F</c>rom lands that see the sun arise
To earth's remotest boundaries,
The Virgin-born today we sing,
The Son of Mary, Christ the King.

<h>B</h>lest Author of this earthly frame,
To take a servant's form He came,
That, liberating flesh by flesh,
Whom He had made might live afresh.

<h>I</h>n that chaste parent's holy womb
Celestial grace hath found its home;
And she, as earthly bride unknown,
Yet calls that Offspring blest her own.

<h>T</h>he mansion of the modest breast
Becomes a shrine where God shall rest:
The pure and undefilèd one
Conceived in her womb the Son.

<h>T</h>hat Son, that Royal Son she bore,
Whom Gabriel's voice had told afore;
Whom, in His mother yet concealed,
The infant Baptist had revealed.

<h>T</h>he manger and the straw He bore,
The cradle did He not abhor;
By milk in infant portions fed,
Who gives e'en fowls their daily bread.

<h>T</h>he heavenly chorus filled the sky,
The Angels sang to God on high,
What time to shepherds, watching lone,
They made creation's Shepherd known.

<h>A</h>ll honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
<r>℟.</r> The Lord is God, and he hath shone upon us.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>O</c>ctávo Idus Ianuárii Luna vicésima octáva. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>E</h>piphánia Dómini.
<h>F</h>loréntiæ natális sancti Andréæ Corsíni, civis Florentíni, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, Epíscopi Fesuláni et Confessóris; quem, miráculis clarum, Urbánus Papa Octávus in Sanctórum númerum rétulit. Eius autem festívitas recólitur prídie Nonas Februárii.
<h>B</h>arcinóne, in Hispánia, item natális sancti Raymúndi de Peñáfort, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, Confessóris, doctrína et sanctitáte célebris. Ipsíus vero festum décimo Kaléndas Februárii celebrátur.
<h>I</h>n Africa commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, in persecutióne Sevéri, ad palum ligáti sunt et igne consúmpti.
<h>I</h>n território Rheménsi pássio sanctæ Macræ Vírginis, quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, iubénte Rictiováro Prǽside, cum in ignem esset præcipitáta et permansísset illǽsa, dehinc, mamíllis abscíssis et squalóre cárceris afflícta, super testas étiam acutíssimas ac prunas volutáta, tandem orans migrávit ad Dóminum.
<h>R</h>hédonis, in Gállia, sancti Melánii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, post innumerabílium signa virtútum, iúgiter cælo inténtus, gloriósus migrávit a sǽculo.
<h>G</h>eris, in Ægýpto, sancti Nilammónis reclúsi, qui, dum ad Episcopátum traherétur invítus, in oratióne spíritum Deo réddidit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.55527ad2c6:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>anuary 6th 2027, the 28th day of the Moon,
<h>T</h>he morrow is the Epiphany of the Lord.
<h>U</h>pon the same 6th day of January, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Florence, holy Andrew Corsini of that city, a Carmelite friar, Bishop of Fiesoli, who was famous for miracles (in the year 1373), and whose name was numbered by Urban VIII. among those of the Saints, whose feast we keep upon the 4th day of February.
<h>A</h>t Barcelona (in the year 1275), holy Raymond of Pehafuerte, of the order of Friars Preachers, famous for his holiness and teaching, whose feast we keep upon the 23rd day of this present month of January.
<h>O</h>n the same day are commemorated many holy martyrs in Africa, who were burnt at the stake in the persecution under the Emperor Severus.
<h>I</h>n the country of Reims, by command of the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy virgin and martyr Macra she was first cast into the fire but remained unhurt, whereupon her breasts were cut off, and she was thrust into a prison and rolled upon sharp potsherds and live coals until she passed away in prayer to be ever with the Lord.
<h>A</h>t Rennes, in Gaul, the holy confessor Melanius (Abbot of Platz) (in the year 511), bishop of that see, who after countless works of power passed gloriously out of this world to that heaven where his heart was already fixed (in the year 530).
<h>A</h>t Geris, in Egypt, the holy hermit Nilammon, who gave up his soul in prayer to God while he was being haled against his will to make him a bishop (fifth century).
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui salútis ætérnæ, beátæ Maríæ virginitáte fecúnda, humáno géneri prǽmia præstitísti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut ipsam pro nobis intercédere sentiámus, per quam merúimus auctórem vitæ suscípere, Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum:
<h>Q</h>ui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.0327e4a1fd:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who, by the fruitful virginity of the Blessed Mary, hast given unto mankind the rewards of everlasting life; grant, we beseech thee, that we may continually feel the might of her intercession, through whom we have worthily received the Author of our life, our Lord Jesus Christ, thy Son:
<h>W</h>ho with thee liveth and reigneth, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.90b020be7c:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui hodiérna die Unigénitum tuum géntibus stella duce revelásti: concéde propítius; ut qui iam te ex fide cognóvimus, usque ad contemplándam spéciem tuæ celsitúdinis perducámur.
<h>P</h>er eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.f1ca92ef5a:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who by the leading of a star didst, as on this day, manifest thine Only-begotten Son to the Gentiles, mercifully grant that we, which know thee now by faith, may after this life have the fruition of thy glorious Godhead:
<h>T</h>hrough the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
